name: Fyodor Dostoevsky
description: A journey through the darkness and light of the human soul — from the brink of execution to the heights of Russian literature. Every choice can lead you to a completely different fate.

scoring.historicalSimilarity: sum of weight for historically matching choices / sum of all event weights * 100
scoring.risk: average risk score of selected choices
scoring.independence: average independence score of selected choices

ending.title: Your Fate: Writer of Depths or History's Forgotten

events.title: Father's Death
events.playerFact: Your father, a strict doctor, dies suddenly and violently. This blow confronts you in your youth with bitter questions about death, justice, and the meaning of life.
events.historicalFact: Your father, Mikhail Dostoevsky, died in 1839, and you faced this loss at age 18, an event that shaped your dark view of life.
events.question: Does this loss drive you toward deep existential questions?

yes.consequence: Grief and unanswered questions draw you toward literature and philosophy.

no.consequence: You accept your father's death and continue your ordinary life, never understanding the depth of suffering.

events.title: Military Academy
events.playerFact: To please your family, you enter a military academy, but soon realize military life is suffocating. Instead, you spend nights studying literature and writing short stories.
events.historicalFact: You studied at the St. Petersburg Academy of Military Engineering, but you were more interested in literature and writing than in your studies.
events.question: Do you prefer military duty over your love of writing?

yes.consequence: You give up writing and continue serving as an ordinary officer.

no.consequence: You take refuge in writing and decide to become a writer, despite family opposition.

events.title: First Literary Success
events.playerFact: You publish your first story and suddenly receive praise from critics. Famous writers see you as a new discovery in literature. But this early success creates heavy expectations for your next work.
events.historicalFact: In 1846, you published the epistolary novel "Poor Folk" and received acclaim from prominent critics like Belinsky.
events.question: Does this success encourage you to continue your literary path?

yes.consequence: You continue writing with greater passion, dedicating yourself to literature.

no.consequence: You fear the pressure of expectations and abandon writing to live in peace.

events.title: The Secret Circle
events.playerFact: You join an intellectual circle discussing radical social ideas. The government sees these meetings as a threat, and all members are arrested. You are among those sentenced to death.
events.historicalFact: You joined the Petrashevsky Circle and were arrested in 1849. After interrogation, you were sentenced to death, but at the last moment, the sentence was commuted to exile in Siberia.
events.question: Facing the firing squad, do you surrender to fear and abandon your beliefs?

yes.consequence: You react with fear and violence, abandoning your beliefs to save yourself, but you lose your self-respect and convictions.

no.consequence: The brush with death transforms you forever, driving you to the deepest questions of existence.

events.title: The Pardon
events.playerFact: At the last moment, your death sentence is commuted to exile in a remote, frozen region. You spend years in a labor camp and then in a distant military outpost. The suffering you witness takes you to the depths of the human soul.
events.historicalFact: Your death sentence was commuted to four years in Omsk prison, followed by military service in Siberia. These years were a defining experience that shaped your worldview.
events.question: Do you turn this suffering into an opportunity for a deeper understanding of humanity?

yes.consequence: You embrace suffering and draw inspiration from it to write stories about the depths of the human soul.

no.consequence: You flee from suffering and become bitter, never returning to writing.

events.title: Return to Life
events.playerFact: After years of exile, you return to the big city. What you saw in prison and what you experienced in those years has transformed you into a different writer. Now you have something to say that no one else knows.
events.historicalFact: In 1859, you returned to St. Petersburg and began writing again with a fresh perspective. Your prison and exile experiences became the foundation of your later works.
events.question: Do you flee from the past and try to live a normal, painless life?

yes.consequence: You flee from the past and try to live a normal, painless life, but the memories never let you go.

no.consequence: You transform your experiences into stories about redemption, guilt, and freedom.

events.title: Death of Wife and Brother
events.playerFact: Within a short time, you lose your wife and beloved brother. These successive losses plunge you into depression and heavy debt. The only thing left for you is paper and pen.
events.historicalFact: In 1864, you lost your wife Maria Dmitrievna and then your brother Mikhail. These emotional blows were accompanied by financial debt and put immense pressure on you.
events.question: Despite everything, do you continue writing?

yes.consequence: Despite everything, you write and transform suffering into art.

no.consequence: You give up writing, drowning in grief and gambling, losing everything you had.

events.title: The Great Novel
events.playerFact: Despite all pressures, you begin writing a novel that encompasses all your existential questions: guilt, redemption, justice, and freedom. The story begins with crime and becomes an exploration of human conscience.
events.historicalFact: In 1866, you published "Crime and Punishment" — a work that made you one of the greatest writers in history and introduced psychological analysis into literature.
events.question: Do you have the courage to write a novel that challenges traditional concepts and delves into the darkest corners of the human soul?

yes.consequence: You write the novel and transform the literary world forever.

no.consequence: You fear writing a controversial work and turn to milder, less provocative stories.

events.title: The Young Secretary
events.playerFact: To complete your next novel, you hire a young secretary to transcribe and organize your notes. But over time, this secretary becomes more than an employee — a loyal partner in life and work.
events.historicalFact: You hired Anna Grigorievna Snitkina as your secretary. She later became your wife and played a crucial role in managing your financial and literary affairs.
events.question: Do you see the young secretary only as an employee and keep your distance?

yes.consequence: You see her only as an employee and keep your distance. Years later, loneliness and financial chaos destroy your life.

no.consequence: A deep relationship forms, and she becomes your support in the hardest days.

events.title: The Final Masterpiece
events.playerFact: Decades of writing, living, suffering, and joy have brought you to a place where you feel you must summarize all your ideas in one great novel. A story about three brothers, each representing an aspect of the human soul: faith, reason, and emotion.
events.historicalFact: In 1880, you published your last and greatest novel, "The Brothers Karamazov" — a masterpiece that gathered all your philosophical and spiritual concerns.
events.question: Do you spend your final years writing a work meant to summarize all your thoughts?

yes.consequence: You write your final masterpiece and immortalize your name in literary history forever.

no.consequence: You fear the pressure of writing a monumental work and turn to shorter, lighter pieces. You never achieve artistic completeness.

events.title: A Superficial Life
events.playerFact: You ignore your father's death and continue your ordinary life. You never confront the depths of suffering and existential questions, so you never write anything lasting.
events.historicalFact: Some of your contemporaries, by ignoring suffering, settled for ordinary, insignificant lives.
events.question: In middle age, seeing the success of your writer contemporaries, do you turn to writing?

yes.consequence: Seeing the glory of literature, you decide to write short stories. Gradually, you become a recognized writer in small literary circles.

no.consequence: You continue your painless life and never pick up a pen. The world never hears your voice.

events.title: The Unknown Officer
events.playerFact: You continue as an officer, living an orderly, uneventful life. You never take up the pen, and your stories are never written.
events.historicalFact: Some graduates of the military academy became unknown officers, and history passed them by.
events.question: In retirement, do you write your military memoirs?

yes.consequence: Writing your military memoirs, you become a bestselling author and your name is recorded in history as a late but impactful writer.

no.consequence: You retire in obscurity, never leaving any trace. History never remembers your name.

events.title: The Forgotten Writer
events.playerFact: Despite the acclaim for your first work, you abandon writing out of fear of criticism. Years later, you are remembered only as a one-work writer on the margins of literary history.
events.historicalFact: Literary history is full of one-work writers who never dared to continue.
events.question: In middle age, seeing the success of your contemporaries, do you return to writing?

yes.consequence: Regretting the past, you pick up the pen again and write a novel that receives critical acclaim. Your name joins literary history, though late.

no.consequence: You never return to writing and live in regret of a lost opportunity.

events.title: The Broken Prisoner
events.playerFact: Before the firing squad, you renounce your beliefs and beg for mercy. You survive but lose your self-respect and convictions. You spend years in shame and humiliation.
events.historicalFact: Some political exiles of that era, by breaking their spirit, never returned to normal life.
events.question: After years of humiliation, do you try to reclaim your lost honor through writing?

yes.consequence: By writing stories about shame and redemption, you gradually become a writer who creates a lasting work from failure. Your name is recorded in literary history as a symbol of return.

no.consequence: You remain in humiliation and silence, never picking up a pen. You tell yourself silence is better than another failure.

events.title: The Unnamed Transformed One
events.playerFact: In prison, you flee from suffering and take refuge in hatred and bitterness instead of writing. After release, you never take up the pen again and spend the rest of your life in anger and loneliness.
events.historicalFact: Some political prisoners, by breaking their spirit, never returned to creativity.
events.question: In old age, seeing literature's impact on society, do you let go of bitterness and turn to writing?

yes.consequence: Regretting years of anger, you write short stories about liberation from hatred. Your works gain attention among intellectuals and save your name from obscurity.

no.consequence: You remain in anger and loneliness until the end, never leaving any trace. The world never learns of your existence.

events.title: An Ordinary, Empty Life
events.playerFact: After returning from exile, you flee from the past and take a clerical job. You spend years in monotony, never saying the words you should have said.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, after experiencing failure, retreated into ordinary lives and vanished from the literary scene.
events.question: Despite your clerical life, do you continue writing short stories at night?

yes.consequence: By writing short stories in your spare time, you gradually become a recognized writer in underground literary circles. After years, your collection is published.

no.consequence: You drown in administrative monotony and never pick up a pen. You live with apparent peace, but you know you silenced a voice.

events.title: The Bankrupt Gambler
events.playerFact: After the death of your wife and brother, you turn to gambling. You lose everything you have, debts pile up, and you never return to writing. Your final days are spent in poverty and loneliness.
events.historicalFact: Some intellectuals of that era destroyed their lives through gambling and extravagance.
events.question: In your final days, do you try to make amends by writing your bitter memoirs?

yes.consequence: By writing the memoirs of a gambler, you create an impactful book that becomes a warning for future generations. Your name remains in history as a writer who returned from the depths.

no.consequence: You die in poverty and regret, never leaving any trace. The world never learns of your suffering.

events.title: The Superficial Writer
events.playerFact: Instead of a controversial and deep novel, you write light, entertaining stories that please the general audience. You achieve financial success but never reach the depths of truth.
events.historicalFact: Literary history is full of writers who chose entertainment over depth and were forgotten.
events.question: In middle age, tired of superficial success, do you seek true depth?

yes.consequence: Regretting years of shallow writing, you write a deep, philosophical novel that earns critical acclaim. Your name is recorded as a writer who returned to himself.

no.consequence: You remain a superficial writer until the end, dying wealthy but with your name only in the margins of forgotten writers.

events.title: Alone Among the Crowd
events.playerFact: You see the young secretary only as an employee and keep your distance. You spend years in loneliness, debts pile up, and your life descends into chaos.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by not accepting help from others, destroyed their own lives.
events.question: After financial collapse, do you turn to your secretary and ask for help?

yes.consequence: By accepting your secretary's help, your life is put in order, and she becomes a loyal companion on your writing path. You spend your final years in peace.

no.consequence: You remain in loneliness and chaos, never letting anyone into your life. You live regretting the lost years.

events.title: Late-Blooming Literary Figure
events.playerFact: Despite your simple life, you turned to writing in middle age and read your short stories in small literary circles. Gradually, you become a known figure among middle-class intellectuals.
events.historicalFact: Some late-blooming writers, by entering literary circles, had a limited but profound impact on their audiences.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this limited but deep impact, despite your national anonymity?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if your name isn't in textbooks, you are immortal in the hearts of the intellectuals you inspired.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lack of national fame, wishing you had pursued wider publication instead of small circles.

events.title: Bestselling Memoirist
events.playerFact: By writing your military memoirs, you have become a bestselling author. Your book is popular among officers and their families, and you are known as the honest voice of the army.
events.historicalFact: Some retired officers, by writing memoirs, achieved literary fame.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this military-literary fame, even though you never wrote a great novel?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your memoirs captured a truth about war and peace that no one else has written.

no.consequence: You live regretting the unwritten novel, wishing you had created fictional stories instead of memoirs.

events.title: Late Return
events.playerFact: Regretting years of silence, you have written a novel that has been critically acclaimed. Though late, your name has joined literary history as a writer who returned from failure.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by returning late, achieved notable success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this late return, despite the lost years?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if late, your voice finally reached the world. Your novel inspires a new generation of writers.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost years, wishing you had taken up the pen in your youth instead of staying silent.

events.title: Return from Shame
events.playerFact: By writing stories about shame and redemption, you have become a writer who created a lasting work from failure. Your name is recorded in literary history as a symbol of return.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by turning failure into art, became influential figures.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this honorable return, despite the years of shame?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing you brought light out of the darkest moments, and your name will shine forever.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost years, wishing you had chosen honor from the start instead of shame.

events.title: Liberation from Hatred
events.playerFact: Regretting years of anger, you have written short stories about liberation from hatred. Your works have gained attention among intellectuals and saved your name from obscurity.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by turning bitterness into art, achieved impactful works.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this late liberation, despite the years of bitterness?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if late, you were able to escape the darkness of hatred and see the light of art.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost years, wishing you had pursued art from the start instead of anger.

events.title: Underground Writer
events.playerFact: By writing short stories in your spare time, you have become a recognized writer in underground literary circles. Your collection has been published after years and has been well received.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by publishing in underground circles, achieved late fame.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this hidden literary path, despite your public anonymity?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing your stories gave voice to intellectuals who never dared to speak.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lack of public fame, wishing you had pursued wider publication instead of the underground.

events.title: Memoirs of a Gambler
events.playerFact: By writing your bitter gambling memoirs, you have created an impactful book that has become a warning for future generations. Your name remains in history as a writer who returned from the depths.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by writing about their bitter experiences, achieved lasting works.
events.question: Are you satisfied that you were able to create a lasting work from the depths of destruction?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if you lost years to gambling, you ultimately built something that will never be destroyed.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost years, wishing you had written instead of gambling from the start.

events.title: Return to Depth
events.playerFact: Regretting years of shallow writing, you have written a deep, philosophical novel that has earned critical acclaim. Your name is recorded as a writer who returned to himself.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by returning from shallowness to depth, achieved artistic success.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this return to depth, despite the lost years?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if late, you reached the truth of art and created a work that will last forever.

no.consequence: You live regretting the lost years, wishing you had pursued depth from the start instead of shallow writing.

events.title: Late Companionship
events.playerFact: By accepting your secretary's help, your life has been put in order, and she has become a loyal companion on your writing path. You spend your final years in peace and with her companionship.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by accepting help from others, achieved late peace.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this late companionship, despite the years of loneliness?

yes.consequence: You live with pride, knowing that even if late, you finally allowed someone into your life, and this companionship enriched your work.

no.consequence: You live regretting the years of loneliness, wishing you had trusted others from the start.

events.title: The Writer Who Became Immortal
events.playerFact: By writing your final masterpiece, you have immortalized your name in literary history. 'The Brothers Karamazov' is recognized as one of history's greatest novels, and future generations know you as the explorer of the human soul's depths.
events.historicalFact: Dostoevsky died in 1881, and after his death, he became one of the most influential writers in history.
events.question: Are you satisfied with this literary immortality, achieved at the cost of a lifetime of suffering?

yes.consequence: You live with deep peace, knowing that your sufferings were the seeds of masterpieces that will shine forever in history.

no.consequence: You regret the lost life, wishing you had experienced more joy instead of suffering. But you know that without suffering, you would never have reached such depth.

events.title: The Writer Who Never Achieved Completeness
events.playerFact: By not writing the final masterpiece, you never achieved artistic completeness. Your short stories remain on the margins of literary history, and your name is recorded as a writer who could have been great but wasn't.
events.historicalFact: Some writers, by not writing great works, remained on the margins of history.
events.question: Do you regret not writing the final masterpiece?

yes.consequence: You live with deep regret, wishing you had had the courage to write that great work. But deep down, you know that fear held you back.

no.consequence: You live with apparent peace, telling yourself what you wrote was enough — but you know the world lost something great.
